items.title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery.
items.author: Sanchez-Puelles, C., Hernandez-Vivanco, A., Grieco, A. et al.

items.title: Magnetic nanoparticle enrichment reveals conserved nitric oxide burst responses in Arabidopsis and wheat
items.summary: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S-nitrosylation. Using Arabidopsis and wheat, we treated plant tissues with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) to simulate a rapid nitric oxide surge. The method was then employed to capture S-nitrosylation dynamics within 24 h after treatment. Our analysis revealed sequence-dependent preferences for cysteines near basic or hydrophobic residues. Proteins showing rapid S-nitrosylation increases were predominantly associated with oxidative stress responses and energy metabolism, consistent with our metabolomic data. Functional studies using wheat TaGR1 mutants identified glutathione reductase 1 as a key regulated target.
items.author: Ji, R., Yang, N., Yu, L. et al.

items.title: N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid Triggers Systemic Acquired Resistance Against Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) in Wheat
items.summary: Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) represents a conserved immune strategy enabling plants to mount long-lasting, whole-plant protection following localized pathogen challenge. In Arabidopsis thaliana, SAR is orchestrated by the mobile immune regulator N-hydroxypipecolic acid (NHP); however, the extent to which NHP defines systemic immune states in polyploid crops remains unclear. Here, we establish NHP as an inducer of systemic immunity in hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum) during infection by the obligate biotrophic fungus Puccinia triticina. Local NHP application conferred robust disease suppression in distal leaves and elicited a temporally structured oxidative response characterized by a distal, biphasic reactive oxygen species (ROS) wave linking local and systemic tissues.
items.author: Sun, S., Formby, S., Craven, C. et al.

items.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
items.summary: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5.
items.author: Flagel, L.

items.title: Endogenous Osteoblast-Osteocyte-Osteoclast Signaling Enables Bone Remodeling, Drug Response, and Cancer Invasion in a Nanoscale Calcified Bone-on-a-Chip
items.summary: Bone homeostasis depends on spatially orchestrated interactions among osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and osteocytes within a unique microenvironment characterized by an extracellular matrix that is mineralized on the nanoscale. Reconstructing these interactions to enable autonomous cell differentiation and tissue remodeling remains a significant challenge in faithfully modeling bone physiology and disease in-vitro. Here, we present an engineered bone-on-a-chip platform that recapitulates the spatial organization of bone-resident cells, the differentiation of immune cells into osteoclasts, and calcified tissue resorption. We demonstrate that nanoscale mineralization of cell-laden collagen hydrogels is associated with ossification- and matrix-associated transcriptional changes and an osteocyte-like phenotype in osteoblast-lineage cells, while establishing a multicellular microenvironment associated with pro-osteoclastogenic RANKL/OPG signaling and supporting osteoclastogenesis and remodeling without the need for exogenous growth factors.
items.author: Sousa, M. G. C., Athirasala, A., Hosseini, M. et al.

items.title: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat
items.summary: Wheat rust diseases threaten global wheat production, highlighting the need for durable sources of resistance. The Lr67-associated G144R substitution in the sugar transport protein gene TaSTP13-D1 confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple fungal pathogens. Here, we used an enhanced prime-editing system (ePPEplus) to introduce this resistance-associated substitution into the three TaSTP13 homoeologs in hexaploid wheat. Using the wheat-compatible JWPE1 vector, we achieved editing frequencies of 84 to 92% across the A, B, and D genomes in regenerated T0 plants. Homozygous edits were recovered in all three homoeologs, including one line carrying homozygous edits across all three genomes. Disease assays showed that edited lines had reduced leaf rust severity and fungal biomass compared with susceptible controls.
items.author: Waites, J., Venado, R. E., Syombua, E. D. et al.

items.title: Primate Saccade Rhythmicity
items.summary: Rhythmic sampling is a hallmark of many sensory systems across diverse organisms. In primate vision, rapid foveating eye movements repetitively sample the visual environment at a rate of approximately 4 Hz. Yet, the observed inter-saccadic interval distributions might equally well be produced by a non-rhythmic stochastic process as by a - putatively variable- rhythmic generator. This raises the fundamental question whether primate visual sampling differs from the numerous examples of rhythmic sampling strategies exhibited across sensory modalities and species. Here, using experiments in humans, macaques, and a marmoset, as well as statistical approaches adopted from studies of temporal structure in neuronal spiking patterns, we show that primate saccade generation is unambiguously rooted in a rhythmic source.
items.author: Näher, T., Zhang, Y., Spadacenta, S. et al.

items.title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
items.summary: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo.
items.author: Park, S. S., Nagy, G. N., Perez Ferrer, I. et al.

items.title: Do altered neural responses during self-reflection converge across psychiatric disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies
items.summary: Altered neural responses during self-reflection have been reported across psychiatric disorders, but it is unknown whether there exist common brain regions across studies. To fill the gap, we conducted a systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies. Through systematic literature search and article screening, we identified 36 studies across 8 diagnostic categories, of which 25 studies were eligible for the ALE meta-analysis. Qualitatively, these studies revealed altered neural response among psychiatric disorders in brain regions include cortical midline and lateral association regions. ALE analyses were conducted separately for self-versus other and self-versus control contrasts, the former identified convergence in the right anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and the latter found converged activation in the left middle frontal gyrus (MFG).
items.author: Zhu, S., Yan, W.-J., Chuan-Peng, H.

items.title: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
items.summary: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner. In this theoretical study, we mainly focus on the processes of spine generation, maturation, and elimination to build a mathematical model of synaptic rewiring, incorporating experimental findings on actin polymerization and depolymerization under the activation of Rho-GTPases mediated by the binding of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) to neurotrophin receptors such as tropomyosin kinase receptor B (TrkB) and the low-affinity-nerve growth factor receptor (p75NTR).
items.author: Tanaka, S., Miyashita, M.

items.title: GradeBins: quality control of bins from synthetic and real metagenomes
items.summary: Genomes reconstructed from metagenomes support studies of microbial diversity and function, but their interpretation depends on how much DNA is recovered and whether foreign sequence is included. Quality can be measured in benchmarks, where contig origins are known, but must be estimated in routine analyses. Here we present GradeBins, which assesses individual bins (contigs assigned to one candidate genome) and summarizes the complete bin set from an assembly. For 6,374 simulated bins, its measurements agreed with AMBER and independent calculations within rounding. In control bins built from 20 kb fragments of reference genomes, GradeBins had lower observed completeness error than CheckM1 and CheckM2 and the highest observed F1 (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) for bin selection.
items.author: Bushnell, B., Bowers, R. M., Villada, J. C.

items.title: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
items.summary: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008). It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species. We tested this hypothesis by combining molecular and morphometric data. Sequence data were obtained from 38 L.
items.author: D'Elia, A. K. P., Soares, L. M. M., Henning, F. et al.

items.title: Centromere divergence and allopolyploidy reshape carnivorous sundew genomes
items.summary: Centromeres are essential for chromosome function, yet how contrasting centromere architectures shape polyploid genome evolution and plant diversification remains unresolved. In monocentric chromosomes, centromeric activity is restricted to one chromosomal region; in holocentric chromosomes, it is distributed along the chromosome length. Hybridization followed by genome doubling can place chromosome sets with different centromeres, repeat complements, and rearrangement histories in the same nucleus. We examined whether such genomic mergers are associated with later chromosome restructuring in carnivorous Caryophyllales, focusing on chromosome-scale assemblies of putatively holocentric Drosera regia and monocentric D. capensis. The two sundews retain broad syntenic continuity and related polyploid ancestry, but their present genomes differ sharply.
items.author: Avila Robledillo, L., Fukushima, K., Salojarvi, J. et al.

items.title: CLASSIFICATION OF PROKARYOTIC DNA METHYLTRANSFERASES BY CATALYTIC DOMAIN TOPOLOGY
items.summary: Prokaryotic DNA methyltransferases (MTases) are essential enzymes that play a crucial role in restriction-modification systems, preventing the degradation of self DNA by restriction enzymes. In addition, they contribute to the regulation of gene expression, DNA repair, DNA replication, and other processes. Here, we propose a novel classification of prokaryotic MTases based on the 3D topology of the catalytic domain, which addresses the limitations of the previous scheme developed by Malone and Bujnicki. The latter, which grouped MTases into categories such as , {beta}, {gamma}, etc., has been in use for over 20 years. We identified seven structural classes (A-G) of MTases by analyzing 38 experimentally determined 3D structures and several AlphaFold-predicted models, and validated the classification against all reviewed DNA MTases from Swiss-Prot.
items.author: Samokhina, M.

items.title: Restriction Enzyme activity under Force determined with autonomous DNA Origami Force Clamps via Gel Electrophoresis
items.summary: Investigating force-depending behaviour in biological systems is a challenging task, with most techniques requiring complex experimental equipment while also often being limited in scalability. We designed a facile force spectroscopy technique using DNA origami-based force clamps that apply forces up to ~40 pN. We validated the approach by using type II endonucleases that have been previously studied quantitatively by single-molecule measurements. Using ensemble measurements based on ubiquitously used agarose gel electrophoresis, we qualitatively observed force-dependent behaviour for EcoRV and force-independent behaviour for BamHI, replicating previous data for these enzymes. Interestingly, we also observed force-dependent behaviour for EcoRI, whose restriction behaviour has been previously described as force-independent.
items.author: Ermatov, A., Matthies, M., Sulc, P. et al.

items.title: Biomolecular design through latent reasoning with RFD4-Proteina
items.summary: Biomolecular design requires finding chemically and geometrically compatible arrangements of interacting atoms and molecules. The complexity of problems which can be tackled by deep learning design models is limited by both the molecular landscape they encompass and their ability to explore that landscape effectively. Here we introduce RFD4-Proteina, which addresses these limitations through intrinsic and extrinsic reasoning within a shared chemical and conformational latent space. The latent space encompasses standard and modified amino acids, sugars, DNA, and RNA, with force-field supervision favoring physically plausible atomic reconstructions. Within this space, intrinsic reasoning uses recurrent refinement to adaptively allocate computation, while extrinsic reasoning guides search with arbitrary constraints such as energetic or geometric criteria.
items.author: Corley, N., Didi, K., Kazman, M. W. et al.

items.title: ISdetector: precise mapping of insertion sequences and associated structural variations from short-read sequencing data
items.summary: Motivation. Repetitive insertion sequences (ISs) and adjacent structural variants (SVs) complicate precise mapping from bacte-rial short reads. Accurate insertion coordinates are important for studying genome evolution and tracking transmission. Results. ISdetector constructs IS-specific references with target copies removed and clusters soft-clipped reads to pinpoint insertion sites. On simulated genomes, it had higher recall and F1 score than ISMapper and MGEFinder. On 19 Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes, it achieved the highest high-confidence F1 score (0.86). On five Shigella sonnei genomes, it performed comparably to ISMapper (F1 score 0.85). It detected 81 of 105 IS6110 copies with associated SVs or complex events, versus 41 (ISMapper) and 12 (MGEFinder).
items.author: Zhou, Y., Lu, B., Zhao, Y.

items.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
items.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints.
items.author: Lee, Y. J., Shah, S., Mantrala, S. et al.

items.title: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
items.summary: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform. Among the 297 pairs above 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), 40.37% of read placements (a read counted against one strain's genome) carried no sequence difference between the two strains, and above 99.9% ANI about three quarters did. Strains of one species also differ in the DNA motifs they methylate.
items.author: Kakabra, K., Claesson, M. J.

items.title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
items.summary: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results.
items.author: Navas Passos, J. A., Pereira Tapia, A., Velez Duncan, C. et al.

items.title: A Rare Constitutional Centromeric Expansion of Chromosome 1 in a Phenotypically Normal Individual: A Comprehensive Cytogenetic Study
items.summary: Constitutional centromeric heteromorphisms are uncommon chromosomal variants that may complicate cytogenetic interpretation. We report a constitutional enlargement of the centromeric region of one chromosome 1 homologue identified incidentally during biological dose estimation in a suspected occupationally exposed individual. Conventional cytogenetics, pancentromeric fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and multiplex FISH confirmed the variant and excluded cryptic chromosomal rearrangements. Analysis of 500 metaphases revealed no dicentric chromosomes. Quantitative assessment demonstrated a centromere to chromosome length ratio of 0.314 plus/minus 0.019 for the enlarged homologue compared with 0.169 plus/minus 0.019 for the unaffected homologue and 0.161 to 0.186 in controls, representing an approximately 1.86 fold increase (t = 28.4, p < 0.0001).
items.author: Shirsath, K. B., Desai, U. N., Notnani, A. et al.

items.title: Fast and background-suppressed DNA-PAINT
items.summary: The speed and resolution of DNA-PAINT imaging is partly limited by the background fluorescence at high imager-strand concentrations. Here, we combine the photoactivatable fluorophore-quencher-DNA probes with the photoactivation, diffusion, and excitation strategy on a spinning disk confocal microscope, decoupling background fluorescence from the imager-strand concentration. This method yields >7-fold faster DNA-PAINT imaging in cells, a ~15 nm localization precision in hydrogels, without using specialized or speed-optimized imager strands.
items.author: Sun, T., Liu, S., Zhang, X. et al.

items.title: Tycholyzer: NanoTemper NT.6 Tycho Analysis Tool
items.summary: NanoTemper Tycho NT.6 is a nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) instrument that enables rapid measurement of apparent protein melting temperatures. Thermal shift assays are widely used to assess protein stability under different conditions, including screening for protein-ligand interactions. These experiments often involve multiple samples, conditions, and replicates collected across several instrument runs, generating datasets that can be cumbersome to organize, compare, and analyze quantitatively. Here, we introduce Tycholyzer, a user-friendly software application that streamlines processing and analysis of Tycho nanoDSF data. Tycholyzer allows users to combine data from multiple runs, inspect and select individual fluorescence traces, and normalize and group replicate profiles for comparison across experimental conditions.
items.author: Ghani, V. G., Boudker, O.

items.title: Minor intron splicing restricts E2F transcription factor activity in RB-deregulated prostate cancer
items.summary: Castration-resistant prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (CRPC-NE) arises in RB1-mutated lineage plastic cells in response to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies. RB1 loss leads to constitutive E2F activation and cylin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor resistance, making it challenging to restrict E2F activity. A post-transcriptional node is that typical E2Fs contain a rare but highly conserved minor intron, processed by the minor spliceosome (MiS). In an in vivo CRISPR screen, we nominate the MiS as the strongest dependency, and U6atac correlates strongest with E2F transcriptional programs in a clinical CRPC cohort. U6atac depletion led to mis-splicing of typical E2Fs, cell cycle arrest, and translation of a minor intron-containing E2F1 isoform (E2F1-MIRI) as a pharmacodynamic biomarker.
items.author: Thienger, P., Paassen, I., Maier, B. et al.

items.title: EcoToxFred: A knowledge-graph-grounded conversational agent for exploring ecotoxicological monitoring and hazard data
items.summary: Assessing chemical risks to aquatic ecosystems requires the joint interpretation of monitoring data, ecotoxicity data, and derived risk indicators, yet such integrated data are rarely accessible to users without database expertise. We present EcoToxFred, an open-source conversational agent that provides natural language access to a curated knowledge graph of chemical monitoring and hazard data for European surface waters. EcoToxFred couples a large language model (LLM) with a Neo4j graph database in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture. An agent interprets user questions, selects tools, translates questions into graph queries, and returns answers as text, tables, or interactive maps, together with the executed query for reproducibility.
items.author: Scheibe, P., Schmid, T. S., Schor, J.

items.title: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
items.summary: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation. It is well known that a design with rapid response to external signals also implies poorer noise mitigation properties. This work investigates the design elements that limit the adverse impact of the multiple feedback loop architecture on noise propagation in the tryptophan system using a frequency response analysis.
items.author: Bavdekar, V., Bhartiya, S., Venkatesh, K. V.

items.title: Combination of in vitro and ex vivo infection models highlights the role of NAD-dependent ADP-ribosylation in Influenza A virus infection.
items.summary: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a major public health concern, causing an estimated 650 000 deaths annually. Although vaccines are available, vaccination coverage is limited and must be repeated annually due to the genetic variability of these viruses. Furthermore, although direct acting antivirals are available, they must be administered as early as possible after infection to be effective. In this context, understanding the metabolic alterations associated with the replication and pathogenesis of IAV could contribute to the development of treatments that promote virus clearance and patient recovery. In this study, we identified the intracellular level of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) as a key factor in the replication of IAV.
items.author: Jacolin, F., Aublin-Gex, A., Vellet, M. et al.

items.title: Azospirillum brasilense and cytidine as combination treatment to enhance drought resilience of peas
items.summary: Aims: This study tested the efficacy of two combination treatments on drought resilience of peas; Azospirillum brasilense Sp7 with the chemoattractant seedling exudate compound cytidine or pea seedling exudate. Methods and Results: Phenotypic characterization revealed that drought tolerance of peas treated with ACyt was 68.9% higher than that of peas treated with the inoculant alone (A). Dry shoot weight of ACyt Drought plants was 30.7% higher than that of plants from the untreated control group NB Drought, drought recovery of ACyt plants was 21.6% better. The treatment with seedling exudate (AEx) was less effective. 16S rDNA analysis revealed that increase in drought tolerance was accompanied by modulation of the rhizosphere.

items.title: Multicellular signaling in reverse cardiac remodeling revealed by integrated bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomics
items.summary: Heart failure results from maladaptive multicellular remodeling triggered by sustained biomechanical stress. Although mechanical unloading can promote reverse remodeling, recovery is frequently incomplete and its mechanistic basis remains unclear. Using a reversible murine pressure-overload model combined with bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomics, we demonstrate that reverse remodeling represents an actively maintained yet constrained multicellular state. Unloading improved cardiac function and partially restored extracellular matrix and metabolic programs, whereas inflammatory and mitochondrial dysfunction signatures persisted. Cardiomyocytes and endothelial cells largely re-established homeostatic transcriptional states, while fibroblasts retained activated programs that dominated residual pathology. Multicellular factor analysis delineated a reversible metabolic stress program and a persistent inflammatory-mitochondrial program coordinated across cardiac cell types.
items.author: Steier, M., Rivero-Garcia, I., Flores, R. O. R. et al.

items.title: Network modeling identifies vitamin B2 control of AIFM2 deficit-driven hepatocyte death in MASLD
items.summary: Drug discovery for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) remains difficult due to network effects. We developed MetaLiver, a public resource to identify druggable nodes within complex interactomes. It incorporates a MASLD-specific knowledge graph that improves bioactive compound contextualization while reducing computing time 18.8-fold. Layering progression-resolved bulk and hepatocyte-specific single-cell MASLD data onto this graph identified the vitamin B2-dependent flavoproteome (FlavProt) as an injury-sensitive network. Induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary human hepatocytes validated that flavin-cofactor replenishment mitigates FlavProt-dependent dysregulation, augmenting metabolic functions under cellular stress. Saturating flavin-cofactor availability blunted human immune cell activation. Clinically, a FlavProt expression score significantly correlated with poor outcomes in retrospectively stratified MASLD patients.
items.author: Weihs, J., Baldo, F., Cardinali, A. et al.

items.title: A dynamic displacement mechanism drives protein import into mitochondria
items.summary: Most mitochondrial proteins are produced in the cytosol and imported through the translocase of the outer mitochondrial membrane (TOM) to reach their final destination. Although this protein entry gate has been structurally characterized, it remains unclear how precursor proteins are handed off from the cytosolic receptor domains to the translocation pore. Here we show that the cytosolic domain of Tom22 - traditionally viewed as the central TOM receptor - acts not as a structured scaffold but as a largely disordered, flexible segment that plays an active role in precursor transfer. Atomic-level structural techniques and in vivo experiments identified a conserved short linear motif that forms a transient -helical element within this disordered domain.
items.author: Sucec, I., Guillerm, U., Schneider, J. et al.

items.title: From Network Topology to Parameterization: An Optimized Model of Endothelial Mechanobiology
items.summary: Endothelial cells integrate biomechanical and biochemical cues to regulate vascular function, which can be modeled using signaling networks. Yet, the extent to which their signaling behavior is determined by network topology versus reaction-specific parameterization remains unclear. We developed a continuous logic-based ordinary differential equation model of endothelial signaling containing 70 species and 123 regulatory reactions assembled from the literature. Model predictions were evaluated against 79 literature-defined responses to imposed wall stress, wall shear stress, hypoxia, or TNF. We first tested whether a single global parameter triplet (describing reaction weight, Hill coefficient, and half-maximal activation) could reproduce these observations. Investigator-selected global parameters reproduced 62/79 responses (78.48%).
items.author: Gueldner, P. H., Irons, L., Warren, J. L. et al.

items.title: Dynamic Hierarchical Interleaved Bloom Filter: An Updatable Index for Large-Scale Fast Sequence Search
items.summary: Motivation: A continued decrease in sequencing costs has facilitated the exponential increase in available sequencing data, with public databases like the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) and Sequence Read Archive (SRA) reaching well in the order of petabases. This has been the incentive to develop more scalable tools for common bioinformatics tasks. One such task is the approximate searching of short sequence patterns like genes or reads in reference data sets. In recent years, a variety of indexing data structures have been proposed for searching large sequencing databases. The state-of-the-art index, the Hierarchical Interleaved Bloom Filter (HIBF), was first-in-class to index one million samples.
items.author: Seiler, E., Willemsen, M., Piro, V. C. et al.

items.title: Ribonucleotide Reductase Inhibition Overcomes FLT3 Inhibitor Resistance in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
items.summary: Internal tandem duplication mutations in FLT3 (FLT3ITD) occur in approximately 30% of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and are among the most common genetic alterations in this disease. FLT3ITD is a major driver of AML and associated with poor clinical outcomes. Although FLT3 inhibitors (FLT3is) have significantly improved outcomes for patients with FLT3ITD+ AML, acquired resistance remains a major barrier to durable clinical benefit. Reactivation of RAS/MAPK signaling, often driven by activating NRAS mutations, is a major mechanism of FLT3i resistance in AML; however, effective strategies to overcome this resistance remain lacking. Here, we identify ribonucleotide reductase (RNR) as a critical therapeutic vulnerability in NRAS-driven FLT3i-resistant FLT3ITD+ AML.
items.author: Tian, Z., Zhang, H., Chatla, S. et al.

items.title: Interpersonal alignment in infra-slow EEG rhythms and bodily signals anticipates mutual recognition
items.summary: Across multiple timescales, neural rhythms coordinate cognitive and physiological processes. Slower rhythms are increasingly recognised as the scale at which autonomic and interoceptive processes are folded into ongoing cognition, a brain&body view of allostatic regulation that is particularly relevant to social interaction. Examining these slow components of the electroencephalogram (EEG) during real-time interaction remains challenging. Here, we recorded infra-slow EEG alongside respiratory, cardiac and skin conductance signals during the perceptual crossing experiment, a social interaction and EEG hyperscanning paradigm. We assessed interpersonal alignment by contrasting trials in which dyads achieved mutual recognition with trials in which they did not, which separates genuine social alignment or recognition from a shared anticipatory context.
items.author: Gravel, N., Guendelman, S., Vidaurre, D.

items.title: Spatiospectral signatures of stomach-brain synchrony
items.summary: While cognitive neuroscience has increasingly recognized the brain-body connection, the temporal dynamics of how the stomach's intrinsic rhythm (~0.05 Hz) modulates human neural activity remain poorly understood. Leveraging high-resolution magneto- encephalography (MEG) and novel high-density electrogastrography (EGG), we provide the first comprehensive spatiotemporal mapping of human gastric-brain coupling at rest. Our circular-linear correlation approach revealed widespread, broadband phase-amplitude coupling between the gastric rhythm and spontaneous cortical oscillations across delta, theta, alpha, and beta bands. Using nonnegative matrix factorization, we identified distinct spatiospectral fingerprints that significantly overlap with the known fMRI-based gastric resting-state network. Functional connectivity analyses based on multivariate Granger causality further showed that these modulation patterns extend to a gastric influence on frequency-specific, directed communication between network components.
items.author: Berther, T., Saltafossi, M., Fehring, J. et al.

items.title: Spreading depolarization, not seizure activity, drives immediate early gene expression in mouse cortex after electroconvulsive stimulation
items.summary: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is a highly effective treatment for several psychiatric disorders, though its biological mechanisms remain unclear. ECT's therapeutic action has traditionally been attributed to the generalized seizure it induces. However, this view is challenged by the recent finding that electroconvulsive stimulation (ECS) can trigger a spreading depolarization (SD) in cortex. Because SD drives massive molecular changes, including expression of the plasticity-related immediate early gene Fos, we hypothesized that SD could be a key mediator of ECT's plasticity-inducing effects. We recorded the neuronal response to ECS in mouse dorsal cortex and observed similar activity to that of patients undergoing ECT.
items.author: Ladret, H. J., Lupori, L., Sieni, L. et al.

items.title: Decoding Articulatory and Phonetic Features: Somatotopic and Sensorimotor Representations in Native and Non-native Consonant Perception
items.summary: Speech perception relies on the integration of auditory and articulatory information, yet the precise role of motor regions remains debated. We combined fMRI with multivariate pattern analyses (MVPA) and behavioral measures to investigate cortical representations of native French and non-native Mandarin consonant perception under clear and noisy conditions. Cross-modal classification analysis showed that articulator-specific features of perceived degraded native bilabial and dental consonants are mapped somatotopically in right lip and tongue motor areas, which are also engaged in consonant production. These representations may support consonant categorization by compensating for degraded auditory input. Representational similarity analysis further revealed that a network encompassing bilateral temporal auditory and frontal motor regions encodes phonetic features, including place and manner of articulation, for both native and non-native consonants.
items.author: Tseng, T., Thibault, S., Krzonowski, J. et al.

items.title: Peripheral detection of viruses shapes brain immunity and behavior in zebrafish
items.summary: Olfactory sensory neurons (OSNs) are constantly exposed to pathogens, including viruses. However, serious brain infection via the olfactory route rarely occurs. When OSNs detect a virus, they coordinate local antiviral immune responses to stop virus progression to the brain. Despite effective immune control in the olfactory periphery, pathogen-triggered neuronal signals reach the CNS via the olfactory bulb (OB). We hypothesized that neuronal detection of a virus by OSNs initiates neuroimmune responses in the OB that prevent pathogen invasion. Using zebrafish (Danio rerio) as a model, we demonstrate viral-specific neuronal activation of OSNs projecting into the OB, indicating that OSNs are electrically activated by viruses.
items.author: Kraus, A., Garcia, B., Ma, J. et al.

items.title: The bile acid receptor TGR5 is a modulator of the bone marrow microenvironment
items.summary: The gut is an emerging regulator of bone marrow (BM) hematopoiesis, with several molecules involved in this communication. Among them, bile acids (BAs) act as a relay between the microbiota and the rest of the body by activating specific receptors, including Takeda G protein-coupled receptor 5 (TGR5). Although TGR5 has potent regulatory effects in immune cells, its role in the BM remains unclear. Here, we show that TGR5 is expressed across hematopoietic populations, including hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells. While TGR5 deficiency did not affect steady-state hematopoiesis, it mildly impaired cell-autonomous short-term hematopoietic reconstitution. In contrast, TGR5 deletion altered the BM microenvironment.
items.author: Alonso-Calleja, A., Perino, A., Schyrr, F. et al.

items.title: Identification of a somatic H3K23me3 methyltransferase SET-19 in C. elegans
items.summary: Histone methylation plays essential roles in modulating chromatin organization and gene expression. H3K23 methylation is a conserved histone modification, yet its biological roles and the enzymes responsible for its deposition remain poorly understood. Here, we show that the loss of set-19 leads to a pronounced reduction in H3K23 methylation in C. elegans, as revealed by quantitative mass spectrometry, western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining. In vitro biochemical assays show that recombinant SET-19 proteins purified from E. coli directly catalyze H3K23 methylation. Genome-wide chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal that H3K23me3 is enriched at heterochromatic regions and that loss of set-19 alters H3K23me3 levels, accompanied by derepression of a subset of genes.
items.author: Xu, M., Fan, Z., Yan, C. et al.

items.title: Can Folding Models Tell Binders from Bluffers? Evidence from POISK: The Patent-Derived Antibody Dataset
items.summary: Structure prediction models are increasingly deployed as zero-shot digital screens in antibody design, operating under the assumption that high folding confidence implies true binding. However, rigorous validation of this premise has been limited by small test sets, narrow target diversity, and the risk of data leakage from training-adjacent structures. Here we introduce POISK: Patent-extracted Organization of Immunoglobulin Sequence Knowledge, a large-scale dataset derived from the US patent literature, comprising 89074 antibody-antigen records extracted from 10110 patents using an LLM-based pipeline. From this resource, we curate a balanced benchmark set of 22494 complexes: 11247 patent-validated binders without a known resolved structure paired with putative non-binders constructed from sequence-similar human repertoire antibodies.
items.author: Tupikina, D., Roncoli, A., Bujotzek, A. et al.

items.title: CellChat Hotspot: A Targeted Approach to Cell Cell Communication Analysis With Spatial transcriptomics Validation.
items.summary: Abstract. In recent years, single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) has enabled the investigation of intercellular communication through Cell Cell Communication (CCC) tools such as CellChat. Despite their potential, these approaches remain challenging to interpret, particularly when global analyses generate complex interaction networks that may include biologically irrelevant signals. To address this limitation, we developed a framework termed CellChat Hotspot, designed to improve the biological interpretability of inferred communication networks. This approach integrates gene set enrichment analysis with a context driven filtering strategy, selecting both genes and cells based on their functional relevance prior to communication inference. Applied to stage II colon cancer data, CellChat Hotspot enabled the identification of condition-specific interaction patterns associated with recurrence.
items.author: Monaco, D., Dioguardi, M., Dipalma, M. et al.

items.title: Combined EZH1/2 and DNMT inhibition overcomes transcriptional barriers imposed by drug-induced epigenetic plasticity in colorectal cancer cells
items.summary: Abnormal DNA methylation patterning is a defining epigenetic hallmark of human cancers and is therapeutically targetable with DNA methyltransferase inhibitors (DNMTi's). However, epigenetic plasticity involving Polycomb Repressive Complex 2 (PRC2)-dependent H3K27 methylation can constrain transcriptional responses to DNMTi's and may contribute to their limited activity in solid tumors. Here, we compare pharmacologic strategies targeting EZH1 and EZH2 in combination with DNMT inhibition in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells and define the molecular features that distinguish EZH2-selective from dual EZH1/2 inhibition. We find that dual EZH1/2 inhibition produces more robust transcriptional activation when combined with DNMT inhibition and more extensive depletion of H3K27 methylation states than EZH2-selective inhibition.
items.author: Chomiak, A. A., Wiseman, A. K., Hrit, J. A. et al.

items.title: Activation of perivascular thermogenic fat improves aortic stenosis
items.summary: Aim: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has - especially in the thoracic area - characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS. Methods and results: We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS. To specifically delineate the role of PVAT activity in AS, we used a pharmacological {beta}3-adrenergic agonist as well as cold exposure in combination with a genetic mouse model with deficient PVAT development.
items.author: Hildebrand, S., Wunderling, K., Siwik-Rog, Z. et al.

items.title: Mathematical Modeling of the Canonical Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Pathway in murine bone-marrow-derived macrophages
items.summary: The aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) is a ligand-activated transcription factor involved in xenobiotic sensing, as well as development, immunity, and tissue homeostasis. AhR signaling proceeds through a canonical and a non-canonical branch. It remains unclear which biochemical steps of the canonical pathway are responsible for distinct ligand specific transcriptional responses. Here, we developed a mechanistic ordinary differential equation model of the canonical AhR pathway in murine bone-marrow-derived macrophages. We calibrated it to time-resolved qPCR measurements of Cyp1a1 and Ahrr mRNA in mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages exposed to three structurally diverse, environmentally relevant ligands with known immunomodulatory activity: 3-methylcholanthrene, indolo[3,2-]carbazole and bisphenol A.
items.author: Wieland, V., Blum, T., Iriady, I. et al.

items.title: Acute FMR1 reduction alters cellular and circuit properties in human cortex
items.summary: Transcriptional silencing of FMR1 results in Fragile X syndrome (FXS), the leading inherited cause of intellectual disability (ID) and autism. Although the impact of FMR1 reduction on cortical function has been studied using the Fmr1-/y mouse model, mechanistic insights from the human brain are lacking. Here we show that acute FMR1 reduction in ex vivo human cortical slices induces transcriptomic changes that are concordant with those observed in FXS patient cortex, identifying many targets not altered in the Fmr1-/y mouse model. Consistent with changes in ion channel expression specifically in human tissue, FMR1 reduction drives increased intrinsic excitability of deep-layer pyramidal neurons and network-level population bursts observed with two-photon calcium imaging.
items.author: Singh, A., Abbaspoor, S., Chung, L. et al.

items.title: Distinct contemplative traditions share a common EEG complexity signature
items.summary: Meditation encompasses diverse practices that train attention inward, unlike externally oriented task states. Which brain-activity features are shared across contemplative practices, which accompany long-term training, and which are tradition-specific remains unclear. We leveraged electroencephalography data from 226 participants: advanced meditators of four contemplative traditions and non-meditating controls. We developed a neurodynamic profiling approach spanning 21 features across four feature families: oscillatory, aperiodic, complexity and timescale. Using extensive machine learning, we found that meditation and task states were reliably separable, driven by a large, uniform drop in complexity during meditation. Meditators differed from controls primarily in timescale dynamics. Traditions exhibited distinct signatures in all feature families except complexity, and meditators neurodynamic profiles identified the contemplative tradition they practiced.
items.author: Shrimali, P., Sasidharan, A., Malipeddi, S. et al.

items.title: Loss of riboflavin biosynthesis leads to accumulation of select aromatic amino acids and loss of infectivity in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
items.summary: Riboflavin biosynthesis is required for in vitro survival of the human pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb). However, despite the lack of a known transporter, growth can be rescued by exogenous riboflavin. The riboflavin biosynthesis pathway is also predicted essential in vivo, but whether riboflavin levels available in the host can support survival has not been directly tested. Here we constructed a set of inducible CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) knockdown and targeted gene deletion strains for known riboflavin biosynthesis genes (ribA2, ribG, ribH, ribC) as tools to characterize riboflavin requirements, uptake, and metabolite changes and to assess in vivo essentiality. We found that riboflavin, but not flavin adenine dinucleotide or flavin mononucleotide, rescued auxotrophy for all strains tested.
items.author: Jaisinghani, N., Arasappan, A., Pradhan, A. et al.

items.title: Measuring satellite arrays of the human Y chromosome from sequencing reads
items.summary: Human Y chromosome satellites vary widely but remain difficult to measure in large cohorts. We developed Yruler, which uses pangenome assemblies to measure satellite lengths, composition and Y dosage from sequencing reads without alignment. Across cohorts, we find lineage-associated differences in centromere and non-centromeric array length, and show that heterochromatin components vary unequally within lineages. Yruler enables population-scale studies of how Y satellite variation relates to health and disease.
items.author: Ortigas-Vasquez, A., Guarracino, A.

items.title: CNVSIM: an interpretable cross-study copy-number reference atlas for cancer subtyping
items.summary: Genome-wide copy-number variation (CNV) profiles provide a representation of structural changes in cancer genomes, but interpreting new profiles with respect to their underlying biology remains challenging. We developed CNVSIM, which organizes CNV profiles into root-specific reference spaces and defines subtypes with chromosome-scale and gene-level signatures. Applied to the Progenetix dataset, CNVSIM established 112 CNV-defined subtypes across 19 cancer roots, supported by 155,881 neoplastic analyses from diverse studies and assay platforms. In the context of diagnostic concepts, these subtypes distinguish genomic architectures and reveal associated differences in somatic mutation patterns, with selected associations supported across cohorts. In practice, CNVSIM enables new profiles to be projected onto the established reference and linked to corresponding reference analyses.
items.author: YU, J., Bardet-Trouilloud, J., Jaeger, S. et al.

items.title: pH-driven dynamics and mechanisms of LNP-mediated siRNA delivery
items.summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of a clinically relevant DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3)-based lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation that exhibits strong short interfering RNA (siRNA, ~21 nt) delivery and potent inhibition of targeted RNAs. Using a combination of coarse-grained and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we characterize the pH-dependent structure of both unloaded and siRNA-loaded LNPs, elucidate the mechanism of siRNA encapsulation, and use these models to propose a plausible mechanism of endosomal escape. Consistent with prior experimental and computational studies, our simulations reproduce an inverted-hexagonal-type morphology in a ~70 nm siRNA-loaded LNPs. For the smaller LNPs mimetics, with only one siRNA sequence, we observe a similar hydrated core as observed in the larger 70 nm LNP model.
items.author: Hossain, K. A., Valerio, M., Medina, P. et al.

items.title: A general method for bootstrapping dense 3D segmentations from sparse 2D annotations
items.summary: Volumetric electron microscopy (vEM) provides unparalleled insight into cellular architecture, transforming our understanding of fundamental biological processes. Precise quantification of volumetric bioimaging data requires 3D instance segmentation, but the time and cost of manual ground-truth annotation present a major bottleneck for training accurate machine learning models. Our lightweight two-stage method generates complete 3D instance segmentations from sparse 2D annotations. A 2D network predicts dense boundaries on every section from minimal 2D labels. A 3D network pre- trained on synthetic data infers connectivity between sections. Across the imaging modalities and biological structures tested, our method generates base segmentations with minutes of human effort per volume.
items.author: Thiyagarajan, V. V., Sheridan, A., Harris, K. M. et al.

items.title: Synaptic pruning, myelination and the emergence of psychiatric disorders in late adolescence
items.summary: Adolescence is an important developmental period during which there are diverse changes in the brain and behavior. Goal-directed behaviors, including working memory, response inhibition, and reinforcement learning, improve during adolescence. At the same time there is substantial pruning of excitatory connections in prefrontal cortex and ongoing myelination of axons, which likely underlie these improvements in behavior. However, psychiatric disorders also become increasingly prevalent in late adolescence. In this study, we develop computational models that suggest a hypothesis for how ongoing changes in the brain can give rise to the increased prevalence of psychiatric disorders including depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), schizophrenia and substance use disorders (SUDs).
items.author: Averbeck, B. B., Brunel, N.

items.title: Assessing multi-eGO Predictions of PDZ2-Peptide Binding across Mutations
items.summary: Accurately predicting how mutations alter protein-peptide binding remains challenging for molecular simulations because both conformational sampling and binding kinetics are computationally demanding. Here, we investigate whether multi-eGO, a hybrid transferable/structure-based atomistic-resolution model previously developed and validated for protein-small molecule interactions, can be transferred to protein-peptide binding. Using the PDZ2 domain of protein tyrosine phosphatase basophil-like in complex with the peptide EQVTAV as a benchmark, we show that multi-eGO, calibrated on explicit-solvent simulations of the complex, predicts the equilibrium dissociation constant of the complex within the expected uncertainty, although binding and unbinding are both accelerated by several orders of magnitude. We then introduce conservative mutations in PDZ2 and in the peptide without additional training for each mutant.
items.author: Ardizzone, C., Stegani, B., Bacic Toplek, F. et al.

items.title: Network modularity reveals context and state-dependent reorganization of time-varying functional connectivity in single-cell resolved neural activity recordings
items.summary: An important goal of neuroscience is to understand how biological neural networks organize activity at multiple scales to enable complex information processing and behavioral output. To address this challenge, large-scale neural activity datasets with increased resolution and wider coverage have become more prevalent across many model systems. However, bridging the gap in scale between changes in pairwise functional connectivity between neurons and changes in brain-wide organization of activity remains a key challenge. In this work, we demonstrate application of modularity-based community detection and network modularity to single-cell resolved recordings, for the first time, as a method to summarize complex changes in time-varying functional connectivity, facilitating comparisons across multiple time windows, recordings, and conditions.
items.author: Moon, S., Liang, J., Lee, H. J. et al.

items.title: Reactive and predictive processes during unpredictable driving collisions in virtual reality: an exploratory immersive study with multimodal neurophysiological monitoring
items.summary: Anticipatory neurophysiological activity before unpredictable emotional events has been reported for decades, but the effects are small, difficult to replicate, and obtained almost exclusively in stripped-down laboratory paradigms. Whether they reflect genuine predictive processes or methodological artifacts remains debated; one rarely tested possibility is that such settings mute it. We examined anticipation in an immersive virtual reality (VR) driving simulation whose collision outcomes were assigned by a quantum random number generator, while EEG, photoplethysmography (PPG), EMG, EOG and inertial (IMU) signals were recorded from a single wireless dry-electrode headset built into the VR display. Sixteen participants passively observed 120 driving sequences ending in a collision or no collision.
items.author: Cannard, C., Yesilbas, D.

items.title: Immersive display systems for simulating natural vision
items.summary: Vision is traditionally studied using simplified stimuli presented briefly near the center of a flat display while subjects maintain visual fixation. This paradigm contrasts sharply with real-world vision, which is immersive, dynamic and strongly influenced by self-initiated actions. Traditional approaches have allowed researchers to systematically study the neural encoding of visual features and the influence of cognitive operations such as attention. However, other methods are needed to study more holistic and first-person perspectives on vision, such as those related to physical space, continuous time, and self-movement. To enable the study of these and other aspects of real-world vision, we developed hemispherical ("dome") display systems for macaque visual neuroscience.
