However, an encouraging average diagnostic performance does not establish reliable performance across clinical settings or justify treatment decisions without further validation. Objective We aimed to assess the predictive performance of imaging-based AI across neoadjuvant strategies, distinguish internal from external validation, and examine limitations affecting interpretation. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through August 7, 2026. Eligible English-language studies evaluated imaging-based AI against pathological assessment of pCR. PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool plus Artificial Intelligence) assessed study quality and risk of bias; GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) assessed certainty for sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR).
items.author: Li Z, Gao X, Zhou J, Wang L, Ren F.

items.title: Depression Screening Positivity, Treatment-Seeking Intention, and Willingness to Take Antidepressants in a Self-Selected Online Sample of Korean Adults: Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study.
items.summary: Background Depression is a prevalent psychiatric condition with functional and socioeconomic consequences. Understanding the barriers to professional help-seeking and treatment acceptance among individuals with depressive symptoms is important. Objective This study aimed to quantify depression screening positivity and examine treatment-seeking intention, willingness to use antidepressants, and perceived barriers among Korean adults, with attention to prior depression-related health care experiences. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in South Korea (March 16-April 5, 2024) via paid social media advertising and messaging app invitations. A total of 1053 adults aged 20 years and older participated in this study. Depression screening was conducted using 2 Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders-derived items, with the endorsement of either item defining a positive screen.
items.author: Kim HN, Kim CM, Park YK, Lee K, Huh Y, Kim W, Kim YS.

items.title: Digital Behavioral Risk Stratification Tool Integrated With HIV Online Self-Testing for HIV Positivity Among Men Who Have Sex With Men: Retrospective Observational Study.
items.summary: Background Due to concerns about privacy breaches and the fear of social stigma, some individuals engaging in high-risk behaviors-particularly men who have sex with men (MSM)-may avoid in-person HIV testing services and instead choose to purchase HIV self-test kits online. Unlike traditional e-commerce platforms that provide self-test kits directly without conducting risk assessments, the "Easy Test Know" platform integrates a structured behavioral risk assessment prior to purchasing an HIV self-test kit, allowing users to be categorized into different HIV risk groups. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the performance of a digital HIV behavioral risk stratification tool integrated with online self-testing among MSM and to determine whether incorporating multidimensional behavioral indicators-particularly the high-risk venue diversity score-could improve the prediction of HIV positivity compared with the platform's existing rule-based risk-scoring algorithm.
items.author: Liu W, Jiang Y, Zhang G, Lv Y.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Fine-Grained Image-Interpretation Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models on Bilingual Radiology Questions: Cross-Sectional Benchmark Study.
items.summary: Background Multimodal large language models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding in radiology and digital health; however, their diagnostic performance across diverse clinical scenarios and fine-grained visual reasoning tasks requires systematic evaluation. Objective The study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and fine-grained visual reasoning performance of 5 multimodal LLMs with bilingual medical imaging questions. Methods This cross-sectional benchmark study evaluated bilingual medical imaging questions using zero-shot prompting on 5 LLMs: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Doubao, Yuanbao, and Llama 4 Maverick. Subgroup analyses by language (English/Chinese), question type (image/text), imaging modality (computed tomography, radiography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, and nuclear medicine), and anatomical system (neurologic, respiratory, cardiovascular, digestive, genitourinary, and musculoskeletal) evaluated intermodel accuracy and intramodel consistency.
items.author: Liu Y, Zhang X, Xu J, Huang M, Xiong Y, Wu W.

items.title: Identifying Metabolic Pathways That Drive Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Study.
items.summary: Background Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a disorder characterized by hyperglycemia that is first recognized during pregnancy due to a mismatch between placental insulin production and increased maternal need, exacerbating insulin resistance. Few studies have systematically examined the metabolic markers and pathways underlying GDM from diagnosis through the postnatal period, including placental metabolic changes through metabolomics studies. Objective This study aims to evaluate the metabolite profiles identified through metabolomics, as well as the associated pathways responsible for hyperglycemia during pregnancy and the postpartum period, in mothers with GDM compared with mothers without diabetes during pregnancy. Methods We plan to recruit an equal number of patients with GDM and age- and BMI-matched mothers without GDM.
items.author: Jebasingh F, Harika LM, Anoop S, Christian M, Daniel S, Benjamin SJ, Rathore S, Selvi RV, Beck MM, Abraham A, Preethi RN, Kolthur-Seetharam U, Sonawane M, Price S, Ilhan Ekinci E, Thomas N.

items.title: Comparative connectomics reveals stage-specific gap junction rewiring that reshapes avoidance behavior
items.summary: Environmental stress can remodel neural circuits, yet how such rewiring generates behavioral adaptation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how dauer-specific circuit remodeling alters nociceptive behavior. We discovered that dauers exhibit significantly shorter avoidance durations than adults. Through comparative connectomics, we observed a substantial expansion of gap junctions within the dauer nociceptive circuit and found that dauer neurons exhibit more transient activity dynamics as a result of this rewiring. Modeling neuronal activity demonstrated that removing dauer-specific connectivity constraints failed to reproduce transient characteristics, validating the functional role of dauer-specific gap junctions. Furthermore, introducing synthetic dauer-specific gap junctions into adults was sufficient to recapitulate dauer-like activity patterns and shorten avoidance duration.
items.author: Choe, D. T., Hall, D. H., Nguyen, K. C. Q. et al.

items.title: Repurposing clofarabine against enteric pathogens via metabolic starvation
items.summary: Enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EPEC/EHEC) cause severe global diarrhoeal disease, exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance. Pathogenesis relies on attaching and effacing lesions, where bacteria generate actin pedestals to adhere, replicate, and destroy intestinal microvilli. To identify novel anti-virulence candidates targeting this process, we conducted a high-throughput phenotypic screen quantifying pedestal formation via high-content fluorescence microscopy. We identified the anticancer nucleotide analogue clofarabine as a potent inhibitor of EPEC growth and pathogenesis. Distinct from its oncology mechanism - inducing DNA chain termination and apoptosis - clofarabine competes with bacterial ATP-dependent processes to impede gene transcription, protein synthesis, and Type III Secretion System (T3SS) function.
items.author: Deans, N. D., Naylor, K. L., Srour, S. et al.

items.title: The nucleus spatially partitions mechanoprotection and mechanosensing
items.summary: Mechanical forces shape cell behavior, but how the nucleus integrates its roles as genome protector and mechanosensor remains unresolved. Here, we dissect the spatiotemporal control of transcriptional response to forces during epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). By combining genome-wide approaches, in vivo nuclear micromanipulation, and quantitative live imaging, we uncover two key properties of nuclear mechanosensing. First, mechanically induced changes in chromatin accessibility and transcription are spatially patterned within the nucleus: genes closest to deformations appear protected, revealing a local shielding mechanism associated with chromatin closure. Second, relocating a gene between chromatin environments is sufficient to alter its mechanosensitivity, challenging the concept of inherently force-sensitive genes.
items.author: Bouzignac, R., Palandri, A., Fritsch, L. et al.

items.title: Integrating Long-Read Structural Variant Analysis with single-nucleus RNA-seq to Elucidate Gene Expression Effects in Disease
items.summary: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genetic diversity, yet how they impact cell types in complex brain diseases remains largely unexplored, partially due to limitations of short-read sequencing. Here, we addressed this fundamental question in Parkinson's disease (PD). generating long-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data for 100 post-mortem brain samples from a PD cohort, constructing a high-confidence catalog of 74,552 SVs. To resolve their functional impact, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from two brain regions from the same samples and focused functional analyses on SVs proximal to genes previously nominated as cis-regulated, potential causal targets of PD-associated GWAS loci.
items.author: Kim, K., Lin, Z., Simmons, S. K. et al.

items.title: Multimodal imaging links molecular identity with nanoscale-resolved 3D cell morphology in opossum cortical cultures
items.summary: In the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), the ability to regenerate after injury drops sharply in the first weeks after birth, but how this change is reflected in cell morphology and organization is still not fully understood. Here we cultivated cortical cell cultures from the gray short-tailed opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and compared cells derived from early postnatal pups (postnatal day 3-6, "Pyoung") with those from older pups (postnatal day 16-18, "Pold"), which differ in their capacity to regenerate after injury. For each culture, we assessed marker-defined cellular composition using fluorescently labeled markers for neurons, glia, and immature/progenitor cells, and characterized their nanoscale-resolved three-dimensional morphology using label-free scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM).
items.author: Ayar, Z., Pongrac, M., Mladinic, M. et al.

items.title: Functional Performance of Electrospun Tissue-Engineered Heart Valve Scaffolds Across Geometries Under Aortic Conditions
items.summary: Electrospun, bioresorbable polymer scaffolds are a promising platform for tissue-engineered heart valves (TEHVs) owing to their fibrous microstructure, tunable mechanics and capacity to support host-cell infiltration and remodeling. Recent in-vitro parametric studies of bioprosthetic heart valve (BHV) geometry have used silicone cast valves to link design parameters to hemodynamic performance and leaflet strain, but the functional behavior of electrospun whole-valve TEHV scaffolds across distinct leaflet geometries and clinically relevant aortic conditions remains poorly characterized. Here, we present an end-to-end workflow in which polycaprolactone (PCL) is electrospun directly onto parametrized, 3D-printed mandrels derived from two established analytical leaflet geometry models, yielding 21 whole-valve scaffolds across four geometries without cutting and assembling flat fiber sheets or suturing of flat fiber sheets.
items.author: Dillinger, H., Saberi, A., Manenti, M. et al.

items.title: A reformulation of the t-test in single-cell transcriptomics dramatically reduces false positives
items.summary: The default differential expression tests in single-cell analysis software provide fast and simple approaches that help practitioners annotate cell populations identified through clustering algorithms. Here, we use theoretical arguments and empirical studies to show that these tests suffer from inflated false positive rates that affect the resulting annotations. We introduce LN's t-test, which tests a novel, asymptotically unbiased log-fold change estimator and avoids these false positives, without compromising speed.
items.author: Kviman, O., Ferreira, P. F., Jun, S.-H. et al.

items.title: Modulating inter-mitochondrial contacts to increase membrane potential for mitigating blue light damage
items.summary: Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) is essential for mitochondrial functions, yet current methods for modulating MMP lack precise spatial and temporal control. Here, we developed an optogenetic mitochondrial tethering system, termed OptoMitoTether, that enables reversible control of inter-mitochondrial proximity with high spatiotemporal precision. Blue light activation induced CRY2PHR oligomerization between adjacent mitochondrial outer membranes, reduced mitochondrial nearest-neighbor distances, and promoted inter-mitochondrial tethering. OptoMitoTether activation was associated with elevated MMP and was associated with lower reactive oxygen species (ROS) and preserved ATP production during prolonged blue light stress. Moreover, OptoMitoTether expression preserved mitochondrial bioenergetic function in human retinal cells and extended lifespan in C.
items.author: Wang, Y., Qiu, K., Zou, W. et al.

items.title: Systematic comparison of gliflozins identifies a selective anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition
items.summary: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown. Methods: We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis.
items.author: Fernandez, L., Brunet, M., Ballongue, E. et al.

items.title: A Double Challenge: Cerebral Blood Flow During Concurrent Breath-Hold and Motor Task
items.summary: Motor activation and breath-holding probe complementary aspects of cerebrovascular function: the response to local neuronal demand and to a global vascular challenge. Combining them tests whether local perfusion responses remain supported when the cerebral circulation must also accommodate a systemic perturbation, potentially revealing constraints that either challenge alone would miss. We used arterial spin labelling (ASL) MRI to investigate whether concurrent breath-holding modifies the regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) response to motor activation. Fourteen healthy volunteers underwent pseudo-continuous ASL at 3T during sequential finger tapping with normal breathing, finger tapping during breath-holding, and breath-holding alone. Each condition included a resting baseline followed by eight 25-second task blocks interleaved with recovery.
items.author: Jakobsen, K., Daiu, M., Critchley, H. et al.

items.title: Higher stomatal density and smaller stomatal size associate with higher grain yield in winter wheat
items.summary: In wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), flag leaf is crucial in determining grain-filling rate and final grain yield. Stomata, microscopic pores on plant surfaces, balance CO2 uptake and evaporative water loss; their numbers and aperture sizes depend on environmental factors. Previous studies have reported associations between stomatal traits and grain yield; mostly under controlled conditions. Our study aimed to investigate flag leaf stomatal anatomical and physiological traits, and their relationships with winter wheat grain yield under field conditions. We measured stomatal density and size, and stomatal conductance on adaxial and abaxial flag leaf surfaces in a three-year field study with twenty-five winter wheat varieties.
items.author: Ivandi, E., Jalakas, P., Tulva, I. et al.

items.title: Time-Resolved Proteomics of a Polyglutamine-Expanded Huntingtin in vitro Cell Model Reveals Early RNA-Regulatory Compensation and Late Respiratory-Chain Remodeling
items.summary: Huntington disease (HD) is caused by a polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein that exerts progressive cellular toxicity. However, the temporal order of pathogenic events, and in particular which changes arise early and which emerge late, remains incompletely defined, despite their distinct therapeutic implications. To examine this trajectory, we profiled the proteome of a huntingtin-expressing cell model at early (72 h) and late (144 h) stages. Rather than a linear progression, the proteome changed in two distinct stages. At the early stage, cells showed increased abundance of RNA-processing, splicing, and protein-synthesis proteins, which may reflect an adaptive response to preserve gene-expression fidelity under stress.
items.author: Sonmez, E., Mutlu, P., Ozlevent, C. et al.

items.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
items.summary: Maintaining multiple items in working memory (WM) requires the allocation of limited resources, which may involve prioritizing individual items over others. Previous work has suggested that attentional prioritization can vary rhythmically between WM samples, but direct empirical evidence for such temporal fluctuations remains scarce. Here, we recorded eye-tracking and EEG to track the temporal dynamics of multi-item processing while participants maintained up to three object orientations in WM. Whereas EEG encoding was only short-lived, miniature gaze patterns reflected the orientations of all three items throughout the entire WM delay and showed systematic load and serial position effects. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, however, we found no evidence that eye movements alternated between the concurrently maintained items.
items.author: Broehl, F., Bielefeldt, A. A., Linde-Domingo, J. et al.

items.title: OpenDrive: An Open-Source Microdrive for Large-Scale Neurophysiology
items.summary: Neuropixels-NHP probes have ushered in a new era of high-density neurophysiology recording in large animal models. Here, we present OpenDrive, an open-source microdrive system designed specifically for acute insertion of Neuropixels-NHPs. OpenDrive combines a custom motorized microdrive, six-drive control console, and software platform. Compared with commercially available options, OpenDrive offers (1) low cost, (2) precise, accurate, and stable probe movement, (3) scalability to many-probe recording, and (4) open-source hardware designs and software. In our experiments, OpenDrive has already supported recordings from thousands of neurons across a variety of cortical and subcortical structures. By lowering technical barriers and enabling community-driven development with OpenDrive, we aim to accelerate Neuropixels recording in large animal models.
items.author: Stine, G. M., Gabel, J., Watters, N. et al.

items.title: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
items.summary: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. Native tissues preserve extracellular particle organization and heterogeneity that are often lost during dissociation. Using cryofixation-based serial block-face scanning electron microscopy, we generated a nanoscale atlas of NVEPs and EVs across 352 Drosophila antennal olfactory sensilla ([~]70% coverage). Segmentation of more than 7,800 extracellular particles revealed distinct populations differing in morphology, size, electron density, and sensillum-class distribution. Analyses of EV biogenesis identified multivesicular bodies and membrane budding in auxiliary cells. Furthermore, sensilla housing degenerating neurons exhibited marked accumulation of EVs and NVEPs, accompanied by increased auxiliary-cell EV biogenesis.
items.author: Vijayakumar, P., Cauwenberghs, K., Garg, M. et al.

items.title: The MarR-family regulator TilR links biosynthesis of enterotoxin tilimycin with physiologic adaptation in Klebsiella oxytoca
items.summary: Members of the Klebsiella oxytoca species complex (KoSC) are ubiquitous gut colonizers that produce the DNA-damaging enterotoxin tilimycin (TM) as part of their virulence-related program. A MarR-like transcriptional regulator, herein designated TilR, controls expression of the divergently transcribed aroX- and NRPS-operons responsible for TM production. Deletion of tilR resulted in pronounced induction of both operons, elevated toxin production, and increased cytotoxicity - establishing TilR as the key repressor of TM biosynthesis. TilR is encoded downstream of the NRPS operon and binds a 20 bp motif within the aroX-NRPS intergenic region, spatially separated from the predicted promoters driving toxin gene expression.
items.author: Unterhauser, K., Grassmann, A. A., Balachandran, P. et al.

items.title: Detection of bifidobacterial lipoproteins with anti-viral potential in donor human milk
items.summary: Background: Group B coxsackieviruses (CVBs) are involved in triggering type 1 diabetes. Free bifidobacterial lipoproteins (BLps) prevent CVBs cell infection. Our objective is to isolate free BLps potentially released by bifidobacteria in breastmilk and document their bioavailability. Methods: Bifidobacterium breve and B. longum were quantified by qPCR in samples donated to the hospitals biobank (DHM) within two weeks following delivery. BLps were captured onto CV B4, analyzed by SDS-PAGE and competitive ELISA. BLps transport through Caco-2 monolayers was monitored after DHM contact. Titration of anti-CV B IgA was carried out by ELISA. Results: Among the 90 enrolled donors, seven were excluded, 68 donated a unique sample and 15 donated multiple specimens (2 to 12).
items.author: AYARI, S., Sane, F., Piva, F. et al.

items.title: Chemotaxis and motility of Achromatium oxaliferum in response to oxygen, sulfide, and nitrate
items.summary: Bacteria of the genus Achromatium are known for their large cell sizes and intracellular calcium carbonate deposits. Achromatium cells inhabit freshwater, brackish, and marine sediments where they accumulate to high abundances at the oxic-anoxic interface. These bacteria alter their vertical position in the sediment along with daily fluctuations in oxygen concentrations. Yet, the mechanism behind their migration in the sediment remains unknown. In this study, we used chemotaxis assays and time-lapse microphotography to analyze the motility and chemotactic behavior of Achromatium oxaliferum. Microscopic observations revealed that rolling and gliding were the main forms of locomotion exhibited by Achromatium. In absence of any stimulant, the movement appeared to be mostly random and changes in direction frequently occurred.
items.author: Schorn, S., Ionescu, D., grossart, H.-P. et al.

items.title: WHaloForce enables chemigenetic imaging of molecular tension in living cells and animals
items.summary: Piconewton forces borne by individual proteins within complex assemblies underlie cell adhesion, migration, and tissue morphogenesis, yet remain difficult to image in living systems. Here, we introduce WHaloForce, a chemigenetic HaloTag-based tension sensor that converts force-dependent relief of tryptophan-mediated dye quenching into a fluorescence lifetime change. Optical tweezers revealed a switch-like unquenching transition near 5 pN, and cellular measurements demonstrated dynamic responses to actomyosin activity. WHaloForce enabled quantitative tension imaging of diverse force-bearing proteins (vinculin, E-cadherin, -catenin, and laminin) in mammalian cells, mouse tissue, and C. elegans. Bright synthetic dyes made tension measurements possible at endogenous expression levels. In C.
items.author: Wu, D., Morales, E. A., Lee, J. et al.

items.title: Endogenous Mechanical Reporters Encode the Global Mechanical Landscape of Morphogenesis
items.summary: Developmental systems usually comprise multiple genetically programmed morphogenetic events within a mechanically continuous environment, yet how individual processes interact and contribute to the overall mechanical landscape remains unknown. Here, we introduce the concept of mechanical reporter: endogenous tissues function as in situ probes of the embedded mechanical landscape. We exemplified cephalic furrow (CF) migration as a mechanical reporter in gastrulating Drosophila. Using optogenetics and genetics, we revealed that CF displacement reflects the combined effect of both force and tissue mechanical properties. By incorporating condition-specific mechanical landscape into a continuum minimal-response model, we developed a framework to quantitatively predict the reporter dynamics.
items.author: Xu, R., Gao, H., Li, F. et al.

items.title: Shared landscape, divergent genomes: Comparative population genomics of co-occurring flora in an isolated Australian mountain range
items.summary: Understanding how landscape heterogeneity shapes genomic variation is key to conserving biodiversity and evolutionary potential. Yet conservation genomics is typically conducted at the single species level, limiting our ability to identify shared genomic patterns or understand how co-occurring taxa differ in their response to common environmental gradients. We assessed spatial patterns of genomic variation and their associations with geographic and environmental features among populations of nine co-existing plant species with contrasting life-histories and ecological traits across Gariwerd, a threatened biodiversity hotspot in south-eastern Australia. All species exhibited weak overall genetic structure, although the magnitude and spatial distribution of differentiation varied among species.
items.author: Lobos, S. E., Ahrens, C. W., Rymer, P. D. et al.

items.title: Branch-Partitioned Selection Tests Reject Random Labels on Real Genes, Even Against a Null Simulated at the Depth of the Data
items.summary: Comparative genomics often turns a trait into a hypothesis about selection by labelling the branches that carry it and testing them against the rest. We asked how such a test behaves when the labels carry no trait. In three panels of about 50 species, fungi, yeasts and lactobacilli, two of them registered in advance, randomly placed terminal labels on presumed-null single-copy genes were rejected by PAML's two-ratio branch model in 65.9, 68.8 and 88.8% of genes, against a nominal 5%. Referring each real gene to replicates simulated under its own fitted null model did not remove the excess: with a generator matched to the depth of the real alignments, 65.0% (95% CI 53.5-75.3) and 83.8% (73.8-91.1) of 80 genes were still rejected.
items.author: Kim, M., Jae-Ho, S.

items.title: Replicative and chronological epigenetic age track genome instability in opposite directions across cancers
items.summary: Epigenetic clocks are widely applied to tumor tissue, yet clocks trained to predict chronological age and clocks built to count cell divisions measure different quantities, and how either relates to the heterogeneity of methylation change within a tumor remains unclear. Here we compare four mitotic clocks with Horvath pan tissue clock in 506 matched tumor and normal pairs from 13 adult solid cancers and in 1,731 pediatric tumors. We show that mitotic age is higher in the tumor than in matched normal tissue in every adult cancer type, and that this advance is robust to tumor purity and cell type composition.
items.author: Mukherji, A., Chattopadhyay, S.

items.title: Programmable amide bond formation using de novo ligases
items.summary: Amide bond formation is of central importance in the chemical industry, underpinning the synthesis of small bioactive molecules, macrocycles, peptides and their conjugates. Conventional methods of amide synthesis rely on stoichiometric coupling agents and costly protecting group manipulations. While biocatalysis can alleviate some of these challenges, enzymes typically operate across a narrow range of substrates and their adaptation to new coupling partners requires extensive engineering. Here we show that de novo amide ligases featuring a cysteine catalytic triad can be programmed computationally to operate across diverse substrate classes with high selectivity. We first designed complementary peptide ligases to selectively functionalise either the N-terminus or a single lysine residue of a polypeptide sequence containing 36 competing lysines.
items.author: Salike, S., Fluegel, T., Gantz, M. et al.

items.title: SIFT: Syncmer-Informed Selection of Haplotypes for T2T Imputation
items.summary: Genome patching improves the completeness of fragmented assemblies by filling unresolved gaps with sequences from reference genomes. Pangenome panels provide diverse candidate haplotypes for this task, but identifying suitable references efficiently becomes increasingly challenging as these panels grow. We present SIFT, a compressed indexing method for selecting reference haplotypes for genome patching with ImpuT2T. SIFT combines closed-syncmer parsing, phrase-level indexing, and pseudo-maximal exact match (pseudo-MEM) queries. Closed syncmers provide a context-independent parsing rule with bounded distances between consecutive selected positions, enabling consistent parsing of reference and query sequences. We demonstrate that two closed syncmers determine the distance at which they can occur consecutively in any string, so that equal substrings of two parses represent identical sequences and no gap sequence need be stored.
items.author: Ferro, E. A., Varki, R., Lin, M.-J. et al.

items.title: Assessing the Capacity of Genomic Language Models to Generate Informative Embeddings of Viral Genome Fragments
items.summary: Genomic language models (gLMs) trained on large volumes of nucleotide sequences are becoming an alternative to classical methods in metagenomic analysis, particularly for studying genomic "dark matter". In this work, we investigate the ability of four gLMs (DNABERT-2, DNABERT-S, ViraLM, and Evo2-7B) to generate taxonomically informative vector representations of short viral genome fragments. We constructed a balanced reference dataset of viruses based on the ICTV Virus Metadata Resource and compared the representations generated by gLMs with conventional k-mer profiles and MinHash sketches using clustering and neighborhood-based metrics (adjusted Rand index (ARI), precision@k, and CROSS precision@k). On the reference dataset, three of the four gLMs outperformed the 4-mer profile in terms of ARI and precision@5 under the same evaluation protocol.
items.author: Kladchenko, A., Manolov, A., Popov, N. S.

items.title: zsasa: a Zig-based engine for high-throughput solvent accessible surface area at proteome scale
items.summary: Advances in structural and computational biology now yield structures by the hundreds of thousands, from predicted-structure databases to molecular-dynamics trajectories. Solvent accessible surface area (SASA), a long-established descriptor of protein stability, binding, and interfaces, remains central to their analysis. Established SASA tools are still widely used, but each covers only part of what such data now demand in input formats, outputs, and speed. We present zsasa, a fast, full-featured, open-source SASA engine for single structures, proteome-scale collections, and trajectories, usable from the command line or Python. It uses the same algorithms as established tools and owes its speed to the implementation, which makes full use of multicore processors and SIMD instructions while keeping memory use low.
items.author: Nagae, T., Tomii, K.

items.title: Enhanced antitumour activity of combined PD-1 blockade and HER2-targeted therapy is associated with reduced epithelial-mesenchymal transition and extracellular matrix-remodelling signatures in gastric cancer
items.summary: Background The combination of PD-1 blockade, HER2-targeted therapy and chemotherapy improves outcomes in HER2-positive advanced gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. However, chemotherapy can independently alter the tumour microenvironment, making the biological effects of PD-1 and HER2 targeting difficult to distinguish. We therefore investigated how PD-1 and HER2 blockade, alone and in combination, affect tumour growth and associated transcriptional programmes. Methods Immunodeficient NOG mice received human PBMCs by tail-vein injection. Three days later, NCI-N87 gastric cancer cells were implanted subcutaneously. Mice were randomised to vehicle, pembrolizumab, trastuzumab, or combination treatment. Tumour growth was assessed, and bulk RNA sequencing was used to identify treatment-associated changes in gene expression, pathway enrichment, and tumour, stromal, and immune cell-associated signatures.
items.author: Wan, P. K.-T., Peng, S., Zhang, X. et al.

items.title: Curvature-based schedule ordering is preserved in homogeneous and heterogeneous tumors
items.summary: During treatment, dosing protocols with identical total dose may favor one schedule over another depending on how exposure is distributed over time. In homogeneous cell populations, Jensen's inequality has been shown to predict whether continuous or intermittent high-dose followed by low-dose is favored, based on the curvature of the concentration-effect function. Scheduling ordering can be performed based on curvature only: concave functions favor continuous dosing while convex functions favor intermittent dosing schedules with a high time-variance. However, tumors exhibit heterogeneous drug sensitivities, and treatment preferentially eliminates drug-sensitive cells, progressively shifting the surviving population toward greater drug resistance. Whether this treatment-induced selection can reverse curvature-based schedule ordering remains unclear.
items.author: Song, A. H., West, J.

items.title: BAF complexes cooperate with lineage-restricted transcription factors to establish cell-state-specific regulatory programs
items.summary: BRG1/BRM-associated factor (BAF) complexes are essential regulators of chromatin organization and cell identity. Genes encoding BAF subunits are among the most frequently mutated in human cancer. Yet, how disruption of a single subunit gives rise to distinct tumor states remains poorly understood. Atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumors (ATRTs) provide a compelling model, as they are uniformly driven by bi-allelic loss of the BAF subunit SMARCB1, yet segregate into distinct molecular subtypes. Using integrated multi-omics profiling of patient-derived ATRT organoids and primary tumor tissues, we show that transcriptional and chromatin accessibility changes upon SMARCB1 reconstitution are directed by subtype- and lineage-specific transcription factor (TF) repertoires.
items.author: He, J., Rios Arceo, C., Anderson, N. et al.

items.title: Melatonin may be associated with changes in HUWE1, AIM2 and PANoptosis‐related proteins following myocardial ischaemia–reperfusion in male rats
items.author: Sahna E, Aslan G, Demir Boler M, Ozdemir Z, Keskin S, Er B, Sahin K.

items.title: M 4.5 - 16 km SSE of Gaoyou, China
items.summary: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded 16 km SSE of Gaoyou, China. The event happened on 10 November 2026 at 22:15 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.summary: A magnitude 4.5 earthquake was recorded 61 km ENE of Blangpidie, Indonesia. The event happened on 10 November 2026 at 22:09 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 10 km. About 1 people reported feeling it. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.

items.title: M 4.9 - 207 km NW of Port-Olry, Vanuatu
items.summary: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake was recorded 207 km NW of Port-Olry, Vanuatu. The event happened on 10 November 2026 at 19:54 UTC. It occurred at a depth of about 12 km. Magnitude and location can change as the agency reviews the data. The agency event page has the map, updates and safety information.
items.author: USGS

items.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
items.summary: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
items.author: Gerelle Q. Dodson

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch.
items.author: Emre Kutlusan, Yongmin Li

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning.
items.author: Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor et al.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes.
items.author: Alex Shtoff

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns.
items.author: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Jiangweizhi Peng et al.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation.
items.author: Ziang Liu, James J. Kim, Yijia Dai et al.

items.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
items.summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI.
items.author: Kabir Bajaj, Henry W. Lin

items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls.
items.author: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys et al.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.summary: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.
items.author: Yeyuan Liu

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for.
items.author: Daniel Lenton

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly.
items.author: Adi Mashiach

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms.
items.author: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown et al.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.summary: Business process automation runs the same Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) again and again on new inputs. Large Language Model (LLM) agents can follow an SOP written in natural language, but they call an LLM to choose every step of every run, which adds latency and cost at scale. We present ReTrace, which turns an SOP and a few logged agent runs into a reusable workflow in which code, not an LLM, selects the next step. The agent's reasoning, the explanation it writes with each tool call, often states why it took an action; the tool calls alone do not. ReTrace extracts the condition behind each step, merges these conditions across runs into a compact rule document, and generates an executable workflow from it.
items.author: Kaiyuan Hou, Yang Ping Kuo, Indranil Bhattacharya et al.

items.title: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
items.summary: Memory-augmented vision-language-action (VLA) policies are meant to remember what happened. Many of them, however, fill memory by time: they sample frames uniformly across the episode and stamp each frame with its time step. Because time passes even when nothing happens, such a memory may not tell waiting from working. We show that it does not. On the counting tasks of RoboMME, we make the robot briefly pause or fidget its wrist. Such a null event changes nothing the task depends on, yet a released memory VLA counts the interval as work done and stops early. We call this failure phantom progress.
items.author: Chubin Zhang, Bo An

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.summary: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. Yet existing evaluations obscure this search process, making it difficult to understand how LLMs explore the space of research ideas and what limits their progress. We introduce Re-Search, which adapts the format of Twenty Questions to research ideation: given only the research problem of a published paper, a model must rediscover the paper's core idea by asking yes-or-no questions. Built from 200 ICML 2026 papers, Re-Search tracks how a model's idea evolves as it asks questions and receives binary oracle feedback, isolating ideation from execution. Across six recent LLMs, nearly all progress happens within the first 30 of 100 questions, which largely decide how the game ends; after that, most models plateau.
items.author: Muhan Gao, Hangxiao Zhu, Xinqi Su et al.

items.title: Nonperturbative string dynamics in a (2+1)D lattice gauge theory on a superconducting quantum processor
items.summary: Electric flux strings underpin confinement in gauge theories. In two spatial dimensions, their evolution involves competing processes of charge motion, pair creation, and transverse deformation. Accessing these dynamics beyond perturbative limits challenges classical approaches, as entanglement growth restricts the times accessible to tensor-network simulations. Here we use quantum simulation to investigate a (2+1)D Z2 lattice gauge theory with dynamical matter and an explicit magnetic plaquette interaction, spanning strongly confined and nonperturbative deconfined regimes. Using 63 superconducting qubits, including 12 ancillas, we evolve initially localized strings with static or dynamical endpoint charges. Spatially resolved measurements reveal rapid charge and flux spreading in the deconfined regime, enhanced matter occupation in the string interior near the pair-creation resonance, and suppressed spreading at strong electric fields.
items.author: Sanziana Stelea, Anthony Gandon, Francesco Tacchino et al.

items.title: Thin-film lithium niobate integrated photonics at 493 nm
items.summary: Visible and near-ultraviolet light underpins applications from biophotonics to quantum computing, which demand fast control of optical amplitude and phase. Integrated photonics offers scalable control, yet most visible-wavelength platforms lack gigahertz-scale modulation. We demonstrate a thin-film lithium niobate platform at 493 nm integrating grating couplers, beamsplitters, ring resonators, and modulators. Segmented traveling-wave modulators achieve a half-wave voltage--length product of 450 mV$\cdot$cm, $>$20 dB extinction, and bandwidth beyond 50 GHz. Ring resonators show $2.9 \pm 0.2$ dB/cm propagation loss and quantify the platform's photorefractive response. This enables agile visible beam delivery for trapped-ion systems, although photorefraction and substrate uniformity remain key challenges to scaling.
items.author: Nicholas Achuthan, Letícia Magalhães, Xudong Li et al.

items.title: Running out of Field Range: Nonlinear Sourcing of Light Scalars
items.summary: Light scalar fields coupled linearly to the Standard Model are constrained by equivalence-principle tests, fifth-force searches, clock comparison tests, and stellar cooling. These bounds assume that the coupling to ordinary matter can be expanded to linear order for all field values reached. For a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson with decay constant $f$ this fails as soon as the field value reaches $O(f)$. The field around a source then stops growing with the coupling, and in addition the linear coupling of a probe is suppressed depending on its location. We reanalyze all of these bounds for the couplings to photons, electrons and nucleons.
items.author: Abhishek Banerjee, Shourya Mukherjee, Stefan Stelzl

items.title: TanCRAFT: Context-Reasoned Anticipatory Feedback for Assembly Tasks
items.summary: Preventing human error in physical assembly tasks requires assistance systems that can intervene before mistakes are made. This is especially challenging in settings where users are free to choose the construction order and correctness depends on the evolving assembly rather than a fixed next step. We present TanCRAFT, a four-stage real-time predictive assistance system that tracks the scene state, reasons about the current partial assembly, forecasts the near-future motion of manipulated pieces, and intervenes when the predicted placement is incompatible with the target. We instantiate our framework and confirm its effectiveness in a controlled tangram assembly task through offline benchmarks and a within-subject user study.
items.author: Sassan Mokhtar, Lars Doorenbos, Marius Bock et al.

items.title: Finite-Key Readiness and Authentication-Key Replenishment in QKD-Assisted UAV Edge Computing
items.summary: A service that needs fresh quantum keys must wait for key release, and may be denied it, before protected computation starts. We quantify this cost for a trusted stationary UAV serving two ground gateways, each obtaining its keys from one finite-key decoy-state BB84 attempt with parameters fixed in advance. A count-level Monte Carlo model, reproduced by a semi-analytic model, links key acceptance to protected upload, computation, and download, including failed attempts and hover energy. At 26~dB effective optical loss, with authentication hashing at its proxy-benchmarked, near-zero cost, fresh keys raise the 95th-percentile completion time of both tasks from 10.37 to 28.65~s; hover energy grows in proportion.
items.author: Dang H. Le, Ban Q. Tran, Susan Mengel

items.title: Structure of correlations for the single-$j$ model using quantum information theory
items.summary: We say that a system undergoes a quantum phase transition when the mean-field ground state of a given Hamiltonian spontaneously breaks its symmetries depending on the Hamiltonian parameters. It is a widely accepted view that this phenomenon enables the mean-field state to absorb the maximum amount of correlations without losing its mean-field structure. However, it is still uncertain how those correlations are incorporated within the mean-field state and how the correlation structure changes when we get closer to the exact ground state by restoring the symmetries. In this work, we answer these questions by studying the single-$j$ model, which is a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries.
items.author: Javier Faba, Vicente Martín, Luis Robledo

items.title: Quantum Thermal Transistor via Nonlinear Environmental Coupling
items.summary: Thermal amplification enables sensitive control of heat currents, providing a basis for heat management and thermal signal processing in quantum devices. For a harmonic oscillator coupled to emitter, collector, and base thermal reservoirs, we recover the absence of thermal amplification when system-reservoir interactions permit only single-quantum exchange. A controlled weak-nonlinearity expansion, supported by numerical stationary solutions, shows that two-quantum exchange at the emitter enables amplification and predicts its onset. When two-quantum exchange dominates at the emitter and collector, varying the base temperature redistributes populations between even and odd oscillator sectors. This changes the emitter and collector heat currents far more than the base current, enabling large thermal amplification.
items.author: Laiba Hayat, M. Tahir Naseem

items.title: Connecting field-level and n-point function measurements of galaxy bias
items.summary: Precise measurements of galaxy bias parameters are essential for extracting cosmological information from galaxy surveys. Field-level analyses infer bias coefficients at a finite cutoff $Λ$, typically related to the lattice resolution, while $n$-point function analyses typically adopt renormalization conditions defined in the low-$k$ limit. In this work, we use the renormalization group (RG) to relate field-level measurements at different cutoffs and connect them to $n$-point function measurements. We generate mock galaxy fields with a Lagrangian perturbation theory forward model and a galaxy bias expansion, and then measure the bias parameters across a range of cutoffs. We show that the RG predictions describe the measured running and, in the limit $Λ\to 0$, agree with the (tree-level) $n$-point function measurements of first-order $b_δ$ and second-order $b_{δ^2}, b_{{G}_2}$.
items.author: Hsiang-Ming Huang, Henrique Rubira, Fabian Schmidt

items.title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
items.summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit.
items.author: Shauvik Biswas, Sayan Chakrabarti

items.title: Angle-Resolved Reflectance Measurements in the Vacuum Ultraviolet for Metallic Samples
items.summary: The light yield of noble-element scintillation detectors depends strongly on the reflective properties of detector materials in the vacuum ultraviolet (VUV), where optical measurements are scarce. For this reason, we built a custom rotary setup at IFIC, equipped with a monochromator and operated in a gaseous argon atmosphere, to perform angle-resolved reflectance measurements in the specular reflection plane. We describe the setup and its extensive characterization, together with the procedure used to measure the bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) of materials at various angles of incidence, for wavelengths from 128 to 500 nm, covering both the argon (128 nm) and xenon (175 nm) scintillation wavelengths.
items.author: H. Amar, J. Álvarez, X. Arrue et al.

items.title: Dimensional Crossover and Correlated Spin Dynamics in the Chain-Like van der Waals Antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$
items.summary: We report a comprehensive investigation of the magnetic properties and spin dynamics of the chain-like van der Waals antiferromagnet AgCrP$_2$S$_6$ using magnetization, magnetic susceptibility, and $^{31}$P nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR). The magnetic susceptibility exhibits a broad maximum near 250 K, characteristic of strong short-range antiferromagnetic correlations in a low-dimensional system. A classical Fisher-chain analysis gives an effective intrachain exchange scale $J/k_B\approx 140$ K, while a quantum $S=3/2$ nearest-neighbor-chain calculation yields $J/k_B\approx 114$ K. A constrained AF-FM zig-zag-chain calculation is also compatible with the susceptibility, supporting a dominant quasi one dimensional antiferromagnetic exchange scale of order 100 K. $^{31}$P NMR measurements provide microscopic insight into both static and dynamic spin correlations.
items.author: C. S. Saramgi, Y. Shemerliuk, S. Selter et al.

items.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
items.summary: Understanding 4D scenes is a core challenge in visual intelligence, requiring models to jointly capture scene geometry, appearance, and dynamics from partial observations. However, existing approaches are subdivided into feedforward models for direct geometric prediction, and generative models for visual synthesis. We introduce UGG, a unified framework for 4D scene understanding that jointly models RGB video and geometric representations such as depth and camera pose. By assigning different noise levels across modalities and time, UGG formulates visual generation and geometric prediction as conditional completion within a single generative model. This flexible formulation enables the model to learn from diverse, heterogeneous datasets with different subsets of geometric and visual annotations.
items.author: Amani Kiruga, Zhiyi Li, Ruojin Cai et al.

items.title: NASA to Welcome Expedition 74 Astronauts Home at Space Center Houston
items.summary: NASA will welcome home the Expedition 74 crew during a public event at Space Center Houston following their return from a long-duration mission aboard the International Space Station. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams; ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot; and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud‑Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev will share mission […]
items.author: Wendy K. Avedisian

items.title: One Policy for 100 Household Tasks: Our Solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge
items.summary: We describe our solution for the 2026 BEHAVIOR Challenge: 100 long-horizon household tasks in the OmniGibson simulator. We placed 9th on the final leaderboard, the only independent team in the top 10. The core of the solution is a single vision-language-action (VLA) model, one checkpoint for all 100 tasks, built on our 1st-place 2025 solution, which is based on $π_{0.5}$. On the 50 tasks shared with 2025, its Q rises from 0.260 to 0.371; across all 100 tasks it scores 0.392.
items.author: Ilia Larchenko, Gleb Zarin, Atindra Nair et al.

items.title: Two Communities, One Problem: Branch-and-Bound vs. A* for Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling
items.summary: Branch-and-Bound (B&B) and $A^*$ are popular exact search methods originating from Operations Research and Artificial Intelligence, respectively. Although the two methods share fundamental search principles, their different ways of exploring the search space can lead to substantially different computational performance. We investigate these differences using the Resource-Constrained Project Scheduling Problem (RCPSP) as an exemplary problem setting. We first establish the relationships between mixed-integer linear programming, state-action, and timed Petri-net representations. Since B&B and $A^*$ admit numerous algorithmic enhancements, we focus on relatively basic implementations. This allows us to examine the fundamental differences between the methods rather than compare the performance of state-of-the-art solvers.
items.author: Izack Cohen, Dominik Kress, Lara Nehrke et al.

items.title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
items.summary: Quantum algorithms for machine learning, chemistry, and cryptanalysis often assume coherent access to classical data at negligible physical cost. We instead treat data loading as a hardware process and quantify the dynamic energetic cost of a quantum random access memory (QRAM) query on a superconducting processor. Using the metric-noise-resource framework, we relate query fidelity and power to gate duration, relative two-qubit drive strength, and the distribution of attenuation across a multi-stage refrigerator, while accounting for thermal photons and gate errors. We analyze the linear-depth multiplexer and the noise-resilient bucket-brigade architectures, adapting the latter to a native superconducting gate set and refining its fidelity analysis using the fully decomposed gate schedule.
items.author: Joao F. Doriguello, Alessandro Luongo, Harshit Verma

items.title: SIGMO: Sigmoid Gated Interaction-Aware Motion Planning
items.summary: Despite the widespread adoption of autonomous vehicle technologies, reliable navigation within cluttered environments remains arduous due to the necessity of interaction-aware strategies; example scenarios include: narrow passages with multiple agents, lane changing in dense traffic, and crossing unsignalized intersections. These scenarios often require highly proactive strategies, simultaneously demanding interpretability and quick adaptability, which challenge end-to-end and data-driven methods. An effective strategy requires: scalability to multiple agents, adaptability to changes in other agents' behavior, and harmony with surrounding traffic without freezing or becoming overly conservative. To meet these requirements, we present SIGMO, a sigmoid-gated interaction-aware motion planner, with two main contributions.
items.author: Avinash Singh, Manish Saroya, Fatemeh Cheraghi Pouria et al.

items.title: Multidimensional Quantum Block Turbo Codes
items.summary: The theory of turbo iterative decoding was brought into the quantum coding framework through the development of quantum serial turbo codes and quantum block turbo codes. In this paper, we present a theory for multidimensional quantum block turbo codes, a turbo decoding technique for multi layer product codes. We describe its algorithm and simulate the performance for the 3D case on a depolarizing channel.
items.author: Khaled Jebari, Luiz Anet Neto, Ramesh Pyndiah et al.

items.title: Simulating closed- and open-system dynamics of Tavis--Cummings lattices on fault-tolerant quantum computers
items.summary: Tavis--Cummings lattices couple cavities containing several emitters and host polaritonic many-body dynamics whose real-time correlations are costly to compute classically in two dimensions, especially when unequal emitter relaxation or dephasing rates break permutation symmetry. We analyze logical resources for fault-tolerant closed- and open-system simulation of an atom-resolved lattice with $L$ cavities, $N$ emitters per cavity, and photon cutoff $n\_{\max}$, including target observable estimation. Building on ladder-operator block encoding, we construct circuits for photon hopping and local light--matter exchange and combine them to encode the lattice Hamiltonian. By updating source and destination photon occupations in place, the hopping circuit eliminates the auxiliary $L\lceil\log_2(n\_{\max}+1)\rceil$-qubit photon register used by two-register implementations.
items.author: Soumya Sarkar, Rakshit Gharat, Nam Nguyen et al.

items.title: Implementing rapid reset of superconducting qubits with on-chip dissipation
items.summary: Rapid and high-fidelity qubit reset is essential for quantum state initialization and quantum error correction. Conventional reset protocols for superconducting qubits often rely on dissipative elements connected to external circuitry, exposing qubits to thermal noise from higher-temperature environments. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a scalable approach to qubit reset and leakage removal over multiple transmon qubits using dedicated dissipation units comprising resonators coupled to on-chip resistive loads. This architecture provides Purcell protection while isolating the qubits from warmer external circuitry. We achieve a median reset time constant of approximately 48 ns for the $|g\rangle-|e\rangle$ transition, with an effective bath temperature of 30 mK.
items.author: Feiyu Li, Yang Liu, Zhen Yang et al.

items.title: The two-component picture of soft hadron production: Regge exchange, duality, and resonance cascades
items.summary: The fragmentation regions of soft hadronic collisions approach energy-independent limits. Benecke, Chou, Yang, and Yen stated this hypothesis of limiting fragmentation in 1969. Feynman gave it a parton-model formulation the same year. Measurements from the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings (ISR) to the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) still show this approach. Fischer and co-workers interpret the NA49 spectra from the CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) as the sum of a target and a projectile component, each the decay of an excited hadronic system. This review traces the theory behind that two-component picture. It examines the hypothesis that the hadronic tools that predate quantum chromodynamics (QCD) suffice for the soft, non-perturbative domain of QCD.
items.author: Ondrej Chvala
